correctness.rationale: For A=a10^d+b10^j+c (a,b,c in 1..9; 1<=j<d), the raw AA^rev coefficient vector is symmetric with center S=a²+b²+c² and every coefficient <=S by Cauchy–Schwarz, so S<=9 implies carry-free palindrome. Conversely, a 2d+1-digit palindrome forces all carries zero by induction from the two symmetric ends, whence S<=9. The only remaining case is a 2d+2-digit palindrome. Let g=min(j,d-j), h=d-2g. The manuscript excludes g>=3 and g=2,h>=1 by first/last two digits from ac and impossibility of a 2-digit palindromic product of digits (11 has no digit divisor); for g=1,h>=3 it reduces to 729 leading-block possibilities with just two edge candidates, each central block not palindromic. Independently enumerated four residual gap pairs (1,0),(1,1),(1,2),(2,0) times 9³=2916 digit triples with no long palindrome. Thus the exact iff covers all d,j; no finite-grid extrapolation.

broader_coverage.reasoning: A conjectured universal converse would include the three-sparse case if proved; it is not prior verified coverage. The present proof settles only three nonzero digits and should not be presented as resolving the unrestricted conjecture.

evidence: Proposition 14 assumes the expected digit length and then proves no carries; it does not eliminate the 2d+2 case. Long-gap carry bounds and residual exhaustive 2916-case certificate establish this distinct obstruction in three-sparse family.

value.rationale: An exact infinite-parameter three-sparse family of the reversal-product carry-free converse is a motivated boundary of the open general palindrome question. Excluding longer-than-expected palindromic products is the substantive content, not merely reproducing the known carry-free sufficient condition; the classification supplies an exact sharp digit-square threshold.

limitations: Only base ten and exactly three nonzero digits; unrelated to all bases or four-plus sparse factors.
